function.mechanism: Provides physical bulking and texture by water-binding and particle-network effects; can reduce caking and help stabilize dispersed systems.

adi.basis: 2018 EFSA re-evaluation concluded no need for a numerical ADI (equivalent to ADI not specified for celluloses group use conditions).

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern at reported uses and use levels for unmodified and modified celluloses including E460(i) and E460(ii).

fda.cfr_citation: No direct Title 21 CFR listing identified for 'microcrystalline cellulose' in eCFR search; related GRAS cellulose derivatives are 21 CFR 182.1480 and 21 CFR 182.1745 (GMP conditions).

adi.basis: ADI not specified for microcrystalline cellulose (JECFA summary; latest toxicological evaluation 1997).

concerns.summary: Historical concern about persorption of very fine particles led JECFA to retain particle-size related specification controls as a precaution.
key_references: WHO Food Additives Series 40 (JECFA microcrystalline cellulose monograph)

concerns.summary: Some human studies reported gastrointestinal-function changes at high intakes, but JECFA did not interpret these as systemic toxic effects under GMP food use.
key_references: WHO Food Additives Series 40 (JECFA microcrystalline cellulose monograph)

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2018: no genotoxic concern for celluloses group under evaluated uses.
EFSA 2018: no carcinogenic properties detected for microcrystalline and modified celluloses in reviewed data.
JECFA evaluation: no evidence ingestion causes toxic effects in humans when used according to GMP.
Recent EFSA FEEDAP opinions (2020, 2024): safety supported for animals/consumer/environment when meeting food-additive specifications.

adi_exceedance.notes: Numeric ADI not established (ADI not specified / no numerical ADI required), so classic ADI exceedance framing is not directly applicable.

risk_assessment.rationale: Convergent EFSA and JECFA conclusions indicate low toxicological concern at authorized/GMP uses, but residual uncertainties (particle-size precaution history and user-handling data gaps in feed contexts) argue against a strict risk_free label.
key_factors: EFSA 2018: no numerical ADI needed; no safety concern at reported uses.
JECFA: ADI not specified retained; no evidence of toxic effects under GMP use.
No IARC classification signal found for microcrystalline cellulose.
No direct standalone Title 21 CFR listing identified for this exact additive name in eCFR query results.
